name: Horizon-Curve Book (HCB): hourly-native multi-horizon residual forecaster + Gârleanu–Pedersen horizon optimiser + minute-timed execution
mechanism:
DATA FLOW. One streaming pass over the 1-minute `ohlcv` table builds TRUE UTC-hour OHLCV bars (open/high/low/close/volume/trade_count) for every asset, dead coins retained — the same GROUP-BY-over-cursor aggregator as `trader/data.py:150-189` (`aggregate_asset_daily`) with the day key replaced by an hour key; never the `prices_np[::bar_minutes]` stride (`mcts_trader/training/env_factory.py:417-418`), which is what every prior "lower frequency" cell used. PIT universe = the 819 POWERED builder (`trader/data.py:318-392`, `include_dead=True`) with the liquidity gate re-derived at hourly resolution (`trader/data.py:82-90`: zf_max, min_active). Per asset i and hour t, causal features in four hourly-native families, each cross-sectionally ranked per timestamp: F-R returns over {1,2,4,6,12,24,48,72,168}h (residual to the equal-weight market via a trailing 30-day hourly β); F-V range/second-moment: Parkinson/Garman–Klass/Yang–Zhang hourly σ over 6/24/168h windows, range-to-close ratio, realised up/down semivariance and their difference over 24h, jump share (max hourly |r|/σ over 24h), intraday variance-ratio (range-vol / close-to-close vol); F-Q volume: dollar-volume z vs 7d, trade_count z, signed volume (sign(r)×vol z), close-location-in-range (CLV) at 1/6/24h; F-X cross-sectional: dispersion, β, idio-vol, plus UTC hour-of-day one-hots interacted with F-R (session periodicity). TARGET for horizon h ∈ {1,2,4,6,12,24,72,168}h: y_{i,t,h} = (r_{i,t→t+h} − β̂_i r_{mkt,t→t+h}) / σ̂_YZ,i,t·√h — market-residual, vol-standardised (Σw=0 by construction → market-neutral). LEARNED OBJECTS: per horizon, one pooled ridge (single coefficient vector shared across all ~273 assets, squared loss, α by validation) and one shallow LightGBM (depth ≤4, squared loss) — the only learned objects; expanding window, quarterly refit, purge ≥ h + 24h; refits are blended linearly over 7 days so a refit can never force a book turn. Measured on TRAIN/VAL only: per-horizon IC_h, the IC autocorrelation φ_h (signal decay per bar), σ̄_res(h), N_eff(year) = (Σλ)²/Σλ² of the residual correlation spectrum, Σ by Ledoit–Wolf.

CONTROL LAW (closed form, not learned; Gârleanu–Pedersen 2013 Props 2–5). Each horizon forecast is a factor f^h with decay φ_h; the Markowitz portfolio is (γΣ)⁻¹B f_t; the aim scales each factor by 1/(1+φ_h·a/γ) (eq. 15) so fast horizons are automatically down-weighted and slow ones up-weighted — this IS the horizon optimiser: no horizon is "picked", the weights fall out of measured (IC_h, φ_h) and the calibrated cost; and the position is x_t = (1−a/λ)x_{t−1} + (a/λ)·aim_t (eq. 10), a from eq. 9 with Λ = λΣ calibrated so that a full re-rank of the Σ|w|=1 book costs 21 bp of notional. Positions are renormalised to Σ|x|=1, Σx=0, no leverage. A no-trade band of 0.25·σ̂ on |aim−x| per asset absorbs forecast noise (the D77-style deadband, hourly). The position is an exponentially weighted average of past aims (eq. 17), so turnover is bounded by construction ≈ (a/λ)·E|aim−x|, and flat is unreachable unless every forecast is exactly zero. EXECUTION RULE: the GP target is computed at each hour close; the trade for each asset is placed as a taker order at the minute within the following 20-minute window chosen by the audited per-asset `linear_uni` 5-minute forecast (806: IC 0.098 at H=5, `runs/806_predictability_probe/result.md`) — the minute-scale signal is used ONLY as timing, never as a position signal (897 closed it as a book). REFIT SCHEDULE: quarterly, expanding, TRAIN 2019→2023-12 for the frozen OOS 2024-01→2026-03 read.
math:
INPUTS (each stated, each to be replaced by its measured value in the kill instrument): book Σ|w|=1 market-neutral (the `mn_portfolio` convention, `runs/812_mcts_trader/eval_postcost_vs_linear.py:109-123`; 819 gross_cap 1.0, `trader/config.py:100`); cost net = gross − Σ|Δw|·21 bp one-sided per decision (`trader/backtest.py:188-190`); σ̄_res(1h) ≈ 70 bp (alt daily vol 3.5–5%, residual ≈ 75% → ≈3.4%/day → /√24), σ̄_res(h)=70√h bp; N_eff = 15 (unmeasured; gap 7); TC = 1 for the per-decision arithmetic.

(1) Expected gross per decision for w ∝ standardised forecast s (Gaussian cross-section): E[r_p] = IC·σ̄_res(h)·Σs²/Σ|s| = IC·σ̄_res(h)/0.798 ≈ 1.25·IC·σ̄_res(h).
(2) Turnover per decision of a book that follows a forecast with inter-decision autocorrelation ρ_h: T_h ≈ √(2(1−ρ_h)); ρ_h→0 gives 1.41 — exactly 816's measured 1.39–1.41 at EVERY H from 20 min to 1 day (`runs/816_operating_point/PHASE1_RESULT.md`, turnover column), i.e. its 63-minute-lag forecast was uncorrelated across consecutive windows even at 20 min.
(3) Break-even IC per decision: IC_be(h) = 21·T_h/(1.25·70·√h) = 0.24·T_h/√h.
   h=1h: T=1.41 → 0.34. h=4h: T=1.41 → 0.17; T=0.7 (ρ=0.75) → 0.084. h=6h: 0.14 / 0.069. h=12h: 0.098 / 0.048. h=24h: T=1.41 → 0.069; T=0.7 → 0.034; T=0.31 (ρ=0.95, a 5-day-persistent signal) → 0.015.
(4) Book σ per decision s_p(h) = σ̄_res(h)·√(1.57/N_eff) = 70√h·0.324 = 22.7√h bp (annual σ_B ≈ 111·√365 ≈ 21%/yr at h=24). Net per decision needed for +0.97 annualised (√(8760/h) per-decision convention, `trader/backtest.py:128-138`): μ_net = 0.97·22.7√h/√(8760/h) = 0.235·h bp → 0.94 bp at 4h, 1.4 bp at 6h, 5.6 bp at 24h. Hence IC_req(h) = IC_be(h) + 0.0027√h: IC_req(4h,T=1.41) ≈ 0.17; IC_req(4h,T=0.7) ≈ 0.089; IC_req(6h,T=0.7) ≈ 0.076; IC_req(24h,T=0.7) ≈ 0.047; IC_req(24h,T=0.31) ≈ 0.028.
(5) Fundamental-law cross-check (Grinold IR = IC·√BR·TC; BR = N_eff·8760/h): at h=4, IC 0.089, N_eff 15: gross SR = 0.089·√(15·2190) = 16.1; cost per decision 0.7·21 = 14.7 bp vs gross 1.25·0.089·140 = 15.6 bp → net 0.9 bp → net SR 0.93. So at 4h the mechanism must earn a GROSS Sharpe of ≈16 to net +0.97: cost eats 94% of gross. Measured reality: 816 at H=60 (1h) earned gross +2.0/+3.7/+3.3 (full64/clean33/majors15) with T=1.4 → net@21 −107/−121/−81 (PHASE1_RESULT table); at H=240 gross +0.28/−1.76/+2.49 → net −27/−35/−19. The best cross-sectional IC anywhere in the record is 0.151 at 1 min, 0.141 at 5 min, 0.060 at 20 min (806 result.md), and ~0 at 4h with minute features (816, inferred from gross; the log prints no IC). A native-feature IC of 0.02–0.04 at 4h — a good outcome — gives gross SR 3.6–7.2 and net −5 to −1.5 at T=0.7.
(6) Why smoothing does not rescue the band: to net positive at IC 0.03 and h=4 needs T ≤ 1.25·0.03·140/21 = 0.25 per decision, i.e. ρ ≈ 0.97 across 4h → position half-life ≈ 130h ≈ 5.5 days → the harvested signal is the 5-day average of the 4h forecast; GP eq. 15 makes this explicit: a factor with per-bar decay φ gets aim weight 1/(1+φ·a/γ), so a 4h signal traded at a 5-day rate is scaled toward zero. The h-optimum, done honestly, lands at h ≥ 1–3 days, where the requirement (IC 0.028–0.047 at T 0.31–0.7) coincides with the memo's 0.03–0.04 (`lore/fable_direction_memo_2026-09-03.md` §1.3). There is NO interior optimum in 1–6h at 21 bp/side for any IC the record or literature makes plausible; the curve is monotone in h until the daily+ region.
(7) Execution-timing value (cost reduction, not alpha): per-asset `linear_uni` IC 0.098 at 5 min × σ_5min ≈ 20 bp ≈ 2 bp expected per unit traded (≈1.4 bp at 1 min: 0.057×~9 bp; 806 result.md). On a book turning 0.3/day: 0.3·365·2 bp = 2.2%/yr ≈ +0.10 SR on a 21%-vol market-neutral book; on the 60–66%-vol trend book (0.155/day) ≈ +0.02 SR. Upper bound ≈ 0.1 SR; it cannot change the verdict of (4)–(6).
(8) Multiplicity (crude E[max SR_N | H0] ≈ √(2 ln N)/√T_yr, T=2.25 yr OOS): N=1 → 0; N=8 horizons → 1.36; N=48 (8h × 3 feature sets × 2 estimators) → 1.85. Both exceed +0.97: any horizon/feature chosen on the OOS window is noise by default; selection must be in-sample (GP weights from TRAIN/VAL IC and φ) and the OOS read a single pre-committed composite.
profit_source: Forecast — of the FIRST MOMENT: the cross-sectional, market-residual, vol-standardised expected return of each asset over h ∈ [1h, 7d], combined across horizons by measured decay. Secondary and strictly bounded (≤ ~0.1 Sharpe, item 7): cost reduction from timing the taker trade within a 20-minute window using the audited 1–5-minute per-asset first-moment forecast. No risk premium and no rebalancing premium is claimed; the market-neutral construction (Σw=0, residual target) means the book earns nothing unless IC>0 — by the iterated-expectations identity in the loops panel, E[gross] = Σ_t E[w_t·E[r_{t+1}|F_t]].
why_learning: (a) Parameter sharing: one coefficient vector per horizon fitted on ~17.7M asset-hours pooled across ~273 assets; a per-asset closed-form estimator has 1/273 of the data at the same noise, and the market-residual target makes pooling legitimate (the market factor, the one thing that differs most across assets in level, is removed). (b) Dimensionality with shrinkage: ~60 hourly-derived features (range decomposition, semivariance asymmetry, jump share, signed volume, CLV, hour-of-day interactions) whose marginal ICs are each far below detectability; ridge/GBM combine them with shrinkage, which a hand-built rule (819's single sign-of-30d) cannot. (c) Interactions and conditional structure: volume × return sign (the crypto short-term-reversal-conditional-on-volume result, Bianchi–Babiak–Dickerson 2022), hour-of-day × momentum (session periodicity tied to NYSE/LSE/HK hours, Zhong 2026), range-vol / close-vol ratio × trend — these are conjunctive and are what the GBM arm exists for; 811's "nonlinear ≤ linear" holds only at 1–20 min (loops panel item 3; the daily/hourly surface is unmeasured). (d) What is NOT learned, deliberately: the controller (GP is closed form given IC_h, φ_h, Σ, λ) and the horizon choice (falls out of eq. 15). The learned object is exactly the conditional mean the record never measured in this form; nothing else in the pipeline can hide a fitted policy (887/892's failure mode).

bear_positive.argument: Market-neutral by construction (residual target, Σw=0): expected return in BEAR22 equals IC × dispersion, independent of the market's sign, so the book is BEAR-positive in expectation iff IC>0 — which is the whole question, and 2022 is inside the forecaster's TRAIN window (form check only, not evidence). Two conditions make it 'conditional' rather than 'yes': (i) the short leg is real Kraken spot margin: the fee page (fetched 2026-09-05) states margin fees apply IN ADDITION to trading fees — opening 0.01–0.05% plus per-4-hour rollover plus a 2% liquidation fee; on a 50%-short book a 0.02%/4h rollover is ≈0.06%/day on the book ≈ 20%/yr, comparable to the entire 21 bp trading-cost stack at 0.3 turns/day and unmodelled anywhere in this program (GIVEN: 'borrow cost not modelled'); (ii) dispersion in 2022 was high (helps gross) but so were delistings/frozen books on small alts, and the hourly liquidity gate must hold PIT. If borrow is charged honestly, the BEAR22 sign depends on IC clearing an additional ~0.01–0.02 per decision at h=24.

guards: 887 adaptive HOLD: there is no learned policy and no flat attractor — x_t is a deterministic linear functional of the aim (GP eq. 7/10/17), renormalised to Σ|x|=1, so gross stays at 1 unless every forecast is exactly zero; the only flat-producing component (no-trade band / any DRO shrinkage gate) has its flat fraction logged, and the SPEC pre-registers 'median gross < 0.5 or >50% of days flat = FAIL' (the tactics panel's flat rule). 892 re-trim damage: turnover arises only through aim changes passed through the single trading rate a/λ; model refits are blended over 7 days so a refit cannot force a book turn; the book must beat 892's turnover-matched random-aim null (matched-activity walks, `experiments/LEDGER.md:102`) with CI lo > 0 — a book whose turnover is forecast noise fails this by construction; realised turnover is reported per year and decomposed (aim drift vs refit vs renormalisation, the tactics-panel row-2 decomposition). 813 selection luck: the grid (8 horizons × 3 feature sets × 2 estimators = 48 diagnostic cells) is frozen in the SPEC with sha256; GP horizon weights are estimated on TRAIN/VAL (≤2023-12) only and frozen; the OOS 2024-01→2026-03 read is ONE pre-committed composite → SR0(1)=0; the 48 diagnostic cells are graded on IC Newey–West t (lag h bars) with Bonferroni 48 and a 30-day circular-shift placebo (dependence-preserving, zero fitting variance), never on OOS Sharpe. Multiplicity SR0(N) quoted beside every table: SR0(N) ≈ √(2 ln N)/√2.25 yr → N=1: 0.00; N=8: 1.36; N=48: 1.85 — both above the +0.97 bar, so 'best OOS cell' is meaningless by construction and is printed with that label. Per-date IC null SD ≈ 1/√(N_live−1) ≈ 0.06–0.07 (loops panel item 4), N_eff governs breadth only; both reported. Annualisation of h<24 decision series uses the H-strided non-overlapping convention (816's) or NW, never √(8760/h) on overlapping returns.

literature.ref: Gârleanu & Pedersen 2013, 'Dynamic Trading with Predictable Returns and Transaction Costs', Journal of Finance 68(6):2309-2340
literature.claim: Closed-form optimal dynamic trading with several return predictors of different mean-reversion speeds under quadratic costs: trade partially toward an aim portfolio that down-weights fast-decaying signals; commodity-futures implementation with 5-day, 12-month and 5-year return signals beats the best static cost-aware strategy net of costs.
literature.numbers: x_t = x_{t-1} + Λ⁻¹A_xx(aim_t − x_{t-1}) (eq. 7); under Λ=λΣ: x_t = (1−a/λ)x_{t-1} + (a/λ)aim_t (eq. 10), a = [−(γ(1−ρ)+λρ) + √((γ(1−ρ)+λρ)² + 4γλ(1−ρ)²)]/(2(1−ρ)) (eq. 9); aim_t = (γΣ)⁻¹B(I + (a/γ)Φ)⁻¹f_t (eq. 14), per-factor scaling 1/(1+φ^k a/γ) (eq. 15); x_t = Σ_τ (a/λ)(1−a/λ)^{t−τ} aim_τ (eq. 17); 'Its net Sharpe ratio is about 20% better than that of the best strategy among all the static strategies' (p. 2312).

controllability: Fully auditable, no checkpoint: the deployable artifact is (i) 8 ridge coefficient vectors (≈60 numbers each) or 8 shallow GBMs, refit quarterly with a 7-day linear blend; (ii) three scalars/matrices — the trading rate a/λ (eq. 9), the per-horizon aim weights 1/(1+φ_h a/γ) (eq. 15), Λ = λΣ with Σ Ledoit–Wolf — all printed; (iii) the position recursion x_t = (1−a/λ)x_{t−1} + (a/λ)aim_t, renormalised Σ|x|=1, Σx=0, no leverage. Turnover is bounded by construction (≈ (a/λ)·E|aim−x| per hour; target ≤ 0.3 book-turns/day, monitored and decomposed); gross exposure is 1 by construction and flat is impossible unless forecasts vanish; every hour's book is reproducible from the stored forecasts and the three scalars. Kill switches (pre-registered, not learned): trailing 90-day realised IC < 0 on 2 consecutive months → gross halved; realised turnover > 1.5× the SPEC target → trading rate halved; margin rollover cost > 30% of gross → short leg capped. Failure mode visibility: the 887 attractor cannot occur silently; the 892 failure (turnover as noise) is the pre-registered matched-turnover null; the 813 failure (cell picking) is excluded by the single pre-committed composite.
compute: CPU only; GPUs (24 GB or 64 GB) buy nothing here. Data: minute table 24 GB (`docs/infrastructure.md:47`); 897 streamed 120,900,027 rows for its universe/window (`lore/notes_2026-08-19.md:218`); hourly aggregation = one streaming pass with O(1) RAM per asset (`trader/data.py:150-189` pattern), a few CPU-hours, safe_run-wrapped on gpu-server (workstation rule). Panel: ≤ 1200 assets × 24 × 365 × 7.4 yr ≈ 78M hourly bars worst case; the PIT liquid set ≈ 273 assets → ≈ 17.7M asset-hours; 60 float32 features → ≈ 4.3 GB (fits RAM; stream X'X for ridge). Ridge: 60×60 normal equations per horizon per refit — seconds. LightGBM depth ≤4 on ≤17.7M rows × 60 features: ≈10–30 min per fit on 16 cores; 8 horizons × ~20 quarterly refits ≈ 30–80 CPU-hours worst case, ≤ 1 CPU-day with 25% row subsampling. GP: one 273×273 Ledoit–Wolf Σ and one scalar a per refit — trivial. Scoring: `trader.backtest._sharpe(period=60·h)` + block bootstrap n_boot 2000 on ≤ 20k decisions per cell — minutes. Total ≤ 2 CPU-days; hourly panel to disk once (a control table, not training data — consistent with the placement rules).

kill_experiment.design: Pre-registered 'IC(h) × cost curve' on the PIT hourly Kraken panel (dead coins retained, hourly liquidity gate), TRAIN/VAL 2019-01→2023-12, OOS 2024-01→2026-03 (minute coverage end). Step 1 (measurement, 48 diagnostic cells): for h ∈ {1,2,4,6,12,24,72,168}h × feature sets {F-R, F-R+F-V+F-Q, all incl. F-X/hour-of-day} × {ridge, GBM}: per-timestamp cross-sectional Spearman IC on the residual vol-standardised target (`runs/806_predictability_probe/probe.py:547-563` estimator), mean by year, NW SE lag h, Bonferroni 48, 30-day circular-shift placebo; the IC autocorrelation φ_h; σ̄_res(h) measured; T_h of the full re-rank book measured; N_eff(year) from the residual correlation spectrum. Step 2 (arithmetic band kill): compute IC_be(h) = 21·T_h/(1.25·σ̄_res(h)) from the MEASURED T_h and σ̄_res(h) and overlay the measured IC(h)±2SE. Step 3 (single pre-committed composite): freeze GP weights from TRAIN/VAL (IC_h, φ_h, Σ, λ calibrated so a full re-rank costs 21 bp), run the HCB book OOS hourly, grade net@{0,8,21} per-decision Sharpe with block-bootstrap CI, by year (2024/2025/2026Q1), BEAR22 in-sample form check, median gross, turnover decomposition, and the 892 turnover-matched random-aim null. Step 4 (execution timing, paired): the same OOS trades executed at the first minute of the window vs the minute chosen by the audited 5-min `linear_uni` forecast within 20 minutes; report bp saved per unit traded with CI. Step 5: report SR0(1)=0 for the composite and SR0(48)≈1.85 beside the diagnostic table.

Expected outcome. The information is two-sided: K1 closes the intermediate band arithmetically with measured inputs; K2 either produces the smallest deployable market-neutral book or hands TASK_915's D79 consequence its second, independent negative.

honest_odds: P(an interior optimum in the 1h–6h band clears +0.97 net@21, PIT, unseen 2024–26): 1–2%. The arithmetic requires IC_req(4h) ≈ 0.09–0.17 (gross Sharpe ≈ 16 at N_eff 15) against a record maximum of 0.15 at 1 min, 0.06 at 20 min and ~0 at 4h with minute features, and a literature with no quantified hourly cross-sectional crypto IC at all; smoothing the position converts a 4h signal into a multi-day one (GP eq. 15) and thereby moves the question to h ≥ 1d. P(the HCB composite with hourly-derived features clears +0.97 at ANY horizon, i.e. the value sits at 1–7d): ≈ 10%; P(clears the PIT bar +0.56 with CI lo > 0): ≈ 22% — roughly the memo's 10–15% / 25%, shifted down for the truncated OOS (minute data ends 2026-03) and for the unmodelled short-leg borrow cost, shifted up slightly for the richer feature set; conditional on TASK_915 G-A failing on daily features, HCB's odds fall to 3–5%. P(K3 execution timing saves ≥ 1.5 bp/unit): ≈ 35%, worth ≤ +0.1 SR either way. P(the IC(h)×cost curve ends the intermediate-band question two-sidedly, which is the real product of running it): > 90%. I do not flatter this: the mechanism is a well-posed forecaster + closed-form controller whose expected verdict, on the record's own numbers, is 'band closed by arithmetic; daily+ end shares TASK_915's ~10–25% odds'.
open_doubts: Short-leg borrow: Kraken margin opening 0.01–0.05% plus per-4-hour rollover in addition to trading fees (fee page, fetched 2026-09-05) — on a 50%-short book plausibly 10–20%/yr, comparable to the entire 21 bp trading-cost stack at 0.3 turns/day, and charged by no market-neutral OHLC book in this program; the operator's actual tier and margin eligibility are unrecorded (loops panel item 1).

σ̄_res(1h) ≈ 70 bp and N_eff ≈ 15 are assumptions standing in for gap (7); N_eff of the residual panel could be 5 (book σ ≈ 36%/yr, cost drag in SR units halves) or 40 (book σ ≈ 13%/yr, cost drag in SR units nearly doubles) — the sign of the verdict at h ≥ 24h is sensitive to it; at h ≤ 6h it is not.

Minute coverage ends 2026-03, so the hourly OOS window is 2.25 yr and 2026H1 collapses to 2026Q1 unless TASK_899's staged backfill extends the minute table; the daily table to 2026-07 cannot feed hourly features.

Hourly bar integrity on small alts: 907 measured BTC/USD's mid frozen 38.9% of capture TIME (`lore/handoff_2026-09-02_factory_run_50.md:72`); alt hourly bars will carry many zero-return hours and stale prints, so the hourly liquidity gate and the residual β must be re-derived and the forecaster must not learn 'stale price → reversal' as an artefact (entry lag G8, next-bar open execution, mandatory).

GP's quadratic cost is a proxy for the repo's linear cost (`trader/backtest.py:188-190`); the proportional-cost optimum is a no-trade band (Davis–Norman). Realised turnover of the GP book must be measured, not read off a/λ; the calibration 'full re-rank = 21 bp of notional' is a convention that fixes λ but not the realised cost.

Overlapping targets at h=72/168 with hourly steps: NW lag must equal h bars and the per-decision Sharpe must use non-overlapping strides or an autocorrelation-corrected SE; the crude √(8760/h) annualisation in the math section is first-order only.
The 1–5-minute execution-timing signal was measured on a 64-asset 2023–25 survivor universe (806); its per-asset IC on the PIT panel, and on assets with frozen mids, is unmeasured — K3 may read zero.
Two-instrument agreement (882 discipline) is unavailable for hourly books because `eval_vector` is daily; a K2 pass would rest on a single scorer until a daily-resampled replay is run.
TC is set to 1 in the per-decision arithmetic and 0.5–0.7 in the memo's fundamental-law conversion; the honest requirement at h ≥ 24h is therefore 1.4–2× the IC quoted here.

The +0.97 bar is survivor-tilted; the PIT bar is +0.56 with CI straddling 0 (`docs/pathway.md:9-21`) — a MARGINAL K2 outcome should be read against +0.56, and the memo's honesty clause (§6) binds this row too.
